newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after profits taken.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after profits taken.

text.p: COMEX copper settled lower as a round of profit-taking sliced off the morning's gains ahead of the holiday week in the West, traders said.
The weaker close came despite a consensus that prices will remain relatively strong over the next few weeks due to tightness in the LME's January contract.
LME stocks also only rose modestly on Friday, up 2,075 to 117,450 tonnes.
"I look for the market to remain in a relatively narrow range for the remainder of the year, and then begin to pick up as we get into January," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.
March COMEX settled 0.90 cent weaker at 99.40 cents per pound, traded 101.20 to 99.30 cents. Spot December went out 0.70 cent lower at 102.60 cents.
Copper has settled inside a narrow range over the past week, with Friday's close up only 0.10 cent from a week ago.
The cash to three months premium or backwardation on LME remained firm at about $100 on Friday since it doubled during the week.
